subject: Physics
scope_summary: Imported candidate for Gravitation, Free Fall & Planetary Orbits. No authority is carried; every gap below must be authored before this can be admitted.

microtopics.title: Gravitation, Free Fall & Planetary Orbits
entry_assumptions: **Point Mass & Spherically Symmetric Body Constraint**: Newton's Law $F = \frac{G m_1 m_2}{r^2}$ applies strictly between point masses or spherically symmetric mass distributions (Newton's Shell Theorem).

**Areal Velocity & Angular Momentum Conservation**: Kepler's Second Law ($\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{L}{2m} = \text{const}$) holds for any central force because torque about the sun is identically zero ($\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = 0$).
microtopics.inferential_jump: Universal Gravitation Law: $F = \frac{G M m}{r^2}$ with $G \approx 6.674 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$.

teaching_path.action: Gravitational potential energy of two-mass system: $U(r) = -\frac{G M m}{r}$ (reference zero at $r \to \infty$).

Orbital mechanics derivations:
  - Orbital speed: $v_o = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}}$.
  - Escape speed from surface: $v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} = \sqrt{2gR} = \sqrt{2}v_o$.
Kepler's Third Law application: $T^2 = \left(\frac{4\pi^2}{GM}\right) a^3$ for elliptical/circular orbits.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Explaining astronaut weightlessness on the ISS as absence of gravity ($g = 0$).
misconceptions.repair: At 400 km altitude, $g \approx 8.7\text{ m/s}^2$ (about 89% of surface gravity). Astronauts experience apparent weightlessness because they and the station are in continuous free fall together.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Assuming a 10 kg bowling ball accelerates twice as fast as a 5 kg ball in free fall.
misconceptions.repair: Inertial mass equals gravitational mass ($m_i a = \frac{GM m_g}{r^2} \implies a = \frac{GM}{r^2}$). Acceleration is completely independent of the falling object's mass.
